transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (observer), Markus (Ironhelm VP Eng), Samantha (Ironhelm InfoSec), Devon (Ironhelm Cloud)

Summary:
Quick intake to map Ironhelm's compliance gates and deployment constraints. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference workloads; main concerns SOC2/ISO, SSO integration (Okta/SAML), RBAC/audit logs, and BYOK + data residency. They requested SOC2 evidence and a private deployment network sketch and want an SE deep dive next week.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for making the time, we'll just do a quick intro, i'm alex from redwood - ae, and priya (se) is here to do the technical bits. can everyone say name and role?
00:12 Markus: hey i'm markus lee, vp eng at ironhelm, we run the routing platform for freight bookings.
00:16 Samantha: sam ortiz, head of infosec.
00:20 Devon: devon cho, cloud architect.
00:23 Alex: awesome. quick agenda, we want to run through your security must-haves, deployment constraints, and then agree next steps — sound good?
00:31 Markus: yep that's perfect.
00:34 Priya: great, i'll jump in on the infra and encryption bits when needed, but sam — do you want to start with the compliance picture you're pursuing?
00:43 Samantha: sure. we're in the middle of SOC2 type II for our platform and ISO 27001 is on the roadmap. for any vendor we want either SOC2 reports and/or ISO attestations, also SSO via SAML with SCIM for user provisioning, we prefer Okta.
00:58 Alex: yep, understood. we can provide a redacted SOC2 type II report and ISO summary, and we support SAML SSO + SCIM.
01:06 Samantha: great. second big question — key management. we require customer-managed keys for any sensitive PII or customer data stored at rest. is bring-your-own-key or HSM possible?
01:18 Priya: yes, we support BYOK with KMS integration for private deployments; for hosted we have options for customer-managed KMS in select regions. quick note: there are two modes - fully private control plane where keys never leave customer KMS, and dedicated with customer key wrap support — i'll clarify in the follow-up docs.
01:36 Devon: hmm can you clarify that — for hosted you mean we provide a path to use our AWS KMS or GCP CMEK? we need that to be auditable, with key rotation policy we control.
01:47 Priya: yes, we have integrations for AWS KMS and GCP CMEK for dedicated or private. hosted public api tends to use redwood-managed keys by default, but with an enterprise contract we can enable customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in supported regions. rotation policies can be enforced by you, and logs show key usage. we'll send specifics.
02:05 Samantha: perfect. audit logs — we need immutable audit trail for admin actions and model deployments, retention at least 3 years, preferably 7 for some regulatory customers. what's your logging retention and export story?
02:17 Alex: good question. we have per-account audit logs surfaced in the console, can stream to customer S3 and SIEMs via syslog or webhook. retention by default is 90 days in the console but export and long-term retention is supported via log forwarding. devon, is SIEM integration part of your stack?
02:31 Devon: yes we push to Splunk and also to our long-term S3 bucket. must be tamper-evident, and we want hashes for integrity checks in audits.
02:39 Priya: we can forward logs to your S3 with WORM settings or to your Splunk instance. for private/on-prem we can keep logs internal to your environment. note: console-level logs might have event enrichment differences; we'll include mapping.
02:55 Samantha: ok. SSO specifics — we use Okta and want SCIM provisioning for service accounts and role mapping. role-based access control we expect roles: admin, infra, app, auditor with separation of duties. does Redwood support granular RBAC and SCIM provisioning for service accounts?
03:10 Alex: yes, we support role templates and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. for private deployments you can map groups to roles and disable self-serve.
03:19 Samantha: service accounts — we require machine-to-machine credentials rotated automatically and ability to audit when service tokens were used. how do tokens show up in audit logs?
03:27 Priya: tokens appear as service principals in audit logs with associated metadata (ip, region, model requested). rotation can be policy-driven; we also support short-lived tokens and OIDC flows for workloads.
03:40 Markus: latency/cost question — our core routes need sub-200ms p50 for short prompts, but we also have batch jobs. what's the difference between hosted, dedicated, private on latency/cost?
03:51 Alex: hosted is fastest to roll out, but cost per token can be higher and key control is limited. dedicated gives predictable throughput with isolated GPU pools and can be placed in a region you control; private (VPC or on-prem) gives strongest isolation and full key control but requires more ops. Priya can add numbers from benchmark runs.
04:10 Priya: in our perf profiles, dedicated pools achieve around 20-30% lower tail latency under continuous load compared to noisy multi-tenant hosted endpoints because of isolation and optimized batching. private on-prem latency depends on customer infra, but you get GPU locality. we'll share a perf spreadsheet.
04:25 Devon: for private, what's the deployment model — do you run a control plane in your cloud and workers in our VPC, or do you want everything on prem? we have air-gapped data centers in EU.
04:34 Priya: we support a hybrid: customer-managed control plane and worker fleet in your VPC, or a fully air-gapped on-prem package. the on-prem path requires additional ops but is possible; there are some feature tradeoffs (some observability shipped to our console is optional).
04:50 Samantha: data residency — we need all inference logs and embeddings stored in EU for EU customers. can you pin region and ensure data at rest stays in region?
05:00 Alex: yes, we can pin model serving to region and configure data residency for hosted dedicated/private. for dedicated we can guarantee region placement, for hosted we have region selection, and private obviously inherits your locality.
05:12 Samantha: embeddings retention — currently we store embeddings for similarity search. we need the ability to purge embeddings and optionally disable storage — can you support ephemeral-only inference?
05:22 Priya: yes, we have an option for no-persistence mode where KV cache or embeddings are not stored beyond session. but some features (like reranking using stored embeddings) won't be available. we'll document tradeoffs.
05:35 Alex: quick interjection — any legal or procurement gates e.g., contract terms, required DPA clauses?
05:40 Markus: procurement will want a DPA and standard security addendum; we also have cyber insurance that asks for subprocessor lists and incident SLA.
05:49 Alex: we can share the subprocessor list and our incident response SLA.
05:53 Samantha: incident response — what is your breach notification timeline? 72 hours?
05:58 Alex: we have 72-hour notification for material breaches and a playbook; we'll send our IR summary.
06:05 Samantha: do you have penetration test reports or do you engage external pentesters?
06:09 Priya: yes, we run annual pen tests and internal red team exercises; can provide summaries and remediation timelines in redacted form.
06:16 Devon: network constraints — for private we need to open specific ports and minimal outbound. can we get a runbook with required ports and CIDR ranges?
06:24 Priya: we'll produce a deployment checklist with port matrix, NAT requirements, and egress rules.
06:31 Markus: curious about secrets handling for model weights and KV cache, do you encrypt in transit and at rest?
06:36 Priya: yes TLS in transit, at rest encryption via KMS. KV cache encryption can be customer-managed in private deployments. there is also an option to salt or tokenise embeddings prior to storage.
06:48 Samantha: regulatory — do you support audit logs with tamper-evidence and hash chaining?
06:52 Priya: for dedicated/private we can enable append-only logs and export with integrity hashes. hosted by default uses our managed logging but can forward to your storages which you can set to WORM.
07:03 Alex: any blockers for Proof-of-Concept (PoC)?
07:06 Markus: timeline: we want a 6-week pilot to validate latency and security, procurement needs SOC2 docs and a DPA signed. also we'd like to run a short benchmark on a dedicated pool.
07:18 Alex: sounds doable; typical flow: share SOC2, then SE deep dive, then pilot agreement for dedicated pool.
07:24 Samantha: one more — access control for model config changes, we need separation between infra and model ops. can you lock down deployment rollouts?
07:33 Priya: yes, we have rollout policies with canary steps, and RBAC gates to restrict who can promote model versions.
07:40 Devon: do you capture model provenance and code versions for audit?
07:44 Priya: we record model version, build id, config, and rollback history in audit logs.
07:51 Markus: ok. any third-party subprocessors for embeddings or vector DB?
07:55 Alex: we rely on some cloud providers for storage and GPU infra; list will be in subprocessor doc. we don't use external vector DB as a managed service by default — embeddings are stored in our managed object store unless customer configures external storage.
08:13 Samantha: legal will ask about data deletion — can you provide a data deletion certificate for when we terminate service or request purge?
08:21 Priya: yes we can provide deletion confirmation and purge logs; for dedicated/private this is straightforward as data lives in your tenancy. hosted we provide an attestation.
08:29 Markus: are there known limitations around FIPS or specific crypto suites needed by some of our gov customers?
08:36 Priya: we have FIPS-compliant options for cryptography in certain deployment modes; we'll confirm which components are FIPS-enabled and send a matrix.
08:46 Alex: great. let's talk rough dates — sam, procurement needs SOC2 and DPA before pilot; can we aim to get those docs by friday?
08:55 Samantha: procurement wants docs now, but let's say next tuesday to give your team time.
08:59 Alex: ok we'll try for monday/tuesday.
09:02 Priya: i'll schedule the SE deep dive for next week with devon and markus, maybe 60-90 minute technical deep dive.
09:10 Devon: works for me.
09:12 Markus: me too.
09:14 Alex: quick recap and action items — priya will put together a network/deployment checklist; alex will send SOC2 and ISO summary and the DPA template; markus to share traffic pattern; we'll schedule deep dive. any other asks?
09:28 Samantha: also please include a description of how you handle model drift monitoring and quality regression alerts — we need that for SOC2 controls around change management.
09:37 Priya: noted, we'll include an overview of model monitoring and the Optimize toolkit capabilities.
09:43 Alex: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
09:48 Markus: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some acronyms spelled out, small transcription errors expected (e.g., "kay em ess" for KMS, "kv cache" no hyphen).
